deep.reconstruction:
PART 1 (top note, Latin). 'The solution of the equation x^3+2y^3+4z^3-6xyz [=1] must be connected with the summation of the series Σ ε^n/(mm+3nn).' The form x^3+2y^3+4z^3-6xyz is the norm N(x+y·θ+z·θ^2) from Q(θ) to Q, where θ=2^(1/3). Its value-1 representations are the units of Z[θ]; a fundamental unit is 1+θ+θ^2 (1+2+4-6=1). The previous page works with m^2+3n^2=p and a hexagonal lattice of Eisenstein integers. This makes the natural reading that ε is a cube root of unity given by the cubic residue character of 2 modulo the prime m+n√-3. The series is then the cubic Hecke L-series L(1,χ). In modern terms the remark predicts ζ_{Q(θ)}(s)=ζ(s)·L(s,χ)·L(s,χ̄), so the residue (class number times regulator, with the regulator built from log of the unit) is given by |L(1,χ)|^2. This is the analytic class number formula for the pure cubic field Q(2^(1/3)). It is stated as an expectation only; nothing is computed.

PART 2. 'Theorem für die biquadr. Reste.'

Setup.
- Modulus π=a+bi is normalised by a unit so that a≡1 (mod 4) and b≡0 (mod 2). Gauss corrected 'beides nach Mod. 4' to 'jenes nach mod 4, dieses nach mod 2'.
- p=a^2+b^2 is prime and Z[i]/π has p classes.
- 'Smallest residues' are the x+iy with (x+iy)/(a+bi)=ξ+iη, 0<ξ,η<1, i.e. lattice points in the open fundamental square.
- The two diagonals cut the square into four triangles. Multiplication by i acts mod π as (ξ,η)->(1-η,ξ), a rotation by 90° about the centre, so it permutes the triangles cyclically. No nonzero residue lies on a diagonal: ξ=η would force x^2+y^2=2k^2/p.
- Hence the triangle T={η<ξ, η<1-ξ} contains exactly (p-1)/4 residues, a 'quarter system' for Gauss's lemma in Z[i].
- Gauss splits T into A (ξ<1/2) and B (ξ>1/2), so A+B=(p-1)/4.

Struck-out attempts. Two lattice-point (floor-sum) expressions for A-B:
- A-B = ½ab - 4{[a/2b]+[3a/2b]+...+[(b-1)a/2b]};
- A-B = ½ab - a + 1 + 8{[b/a]+[3b/a]+...+[½(a-3)b/a]}.
These are Eisenstein-style counting reformulations. Both are deleted. The first is correct mod 4 but not exactly: for 5+4i it gives 6, while the true value is -2.

Conjectured closed forms.
- A=(p-1)/8+b/4 and B=(p-1)/8-b/4. These are integers because (a^2-1)/8 and b(b+2)/8 are integers for a odd, b even.
- Hence A-B=b/2.
- My check by direct enumeration: exact for 1±2i, -3+2i, 1+4i, 5+2i, 1+6i (A,B = 1,0; 2,1; 3,1; 4,3; 6,3).
- It fails for 5+4i (p=41): A=4, B=6, whereas the formula gives A=6, B=4.

Characters via Gauss's lemma. Gauss reads off the biquadratic characters as i^(exponent), exponents mod 4:
- for 1+i: 2B-A = (p-1)/8 - 3b/4;
- for 1-i: B-2A = -(p-1)/8 - 3b/4;
- for 2: A-B = b/2.
The first two follow algebraically from the A,B formulas. Since 2=(1+i)(1-i), they must add up to the exponent for 2: indeed (2B-A)+(B-2A) = -3(A-B) ≡ A-B (mod 4). The 2-exponent b/2 ≡ ab/2 (mod 4) agrees with the known law (2/π)_4 = i^(ab/2), and A-B ≡ b/2 (mod 4) holds even when the exact formula fails (41: -2≡2).

The correct quantity for 1+i. Gauss then isolates 'the quantity on which the class of 1+i depends'. He writes it as the sum of three lines: (1/8 b^2 - 1/2 b - 1/4 ab + 1/4 a - 1/4) + (1/8 a^2 - 1/4 a + 1/8) + (1/2 a - 1/2). He simplifies it:
- Q = 1/8 a^2 - 1/4 ab + 1/8 b^2 + 1/2 a - 1/2 b - 5/8
- = (a-b)^2/8 + (a-b)/2 - 5/8
- = (a-b+2)^2/8 - 9/8
- = (a-b-1)(a-b+5)/8.
All three equalities are correct. My checks show Q ≡ the classical exponent for 1+i (mod 4):
- Gauss 1832: (a-b-b^2-1)/4 for b≡0 mod 4;
- for b≡2 mod 4, using the Gauss-primary associate -π: (-a+b-b^2-1)/4.
- Examples: 1+4i:3; 5+4i:0; 1+2i:3; -3+2i:0; 5+2i:2; 1+6i:0.

Why the closed form fails (the marginal note). Comparing with F = (p-1)/8 - 3b/4 (written at the bottom as 1/8 aa + 1/8 bb - 3/4 b - 1/8), my algebra gives Q - F = -(a-1)(b-2)/4. Since 4|(a-1) and 2|(b-2), (a-1)(b-2) is always divisible by 8. So F ≡ Q (mod 4) iff 16|(a-1)(b-2). It fails exactly when (a-1)/4 is odd and b/2 is even. That is precisely the marginal note ('...¼(a-1)(b-2)... durch 16 theilbar ... oder wenn ¼(a-1) ungerade und ½b gerade ... bei 5+4i'). 5+4i (p=41) is the smallest prime where it fails, the counterexample I found independently.

'Allgemeiner ist':
- E1 = 3/8 a^2 + 1/4 ab - 3/8 b^2 - 3/8. This is an integer and agrees with Q mod 4 in all tested cases. With the side congruences ¼(aa-1)≡0 etc., Gauss appears to reduce among equivalent quadratic forms of the exponent.
- E2 = -1/8 a^2 + 1/4 ab - 3/8 b^2 - 7/8 (as transcribed) satisfies E1 - E2 = (a^2+1)/2 ≡ 1 (mod 4). So as read it is off by one; see errors.

The last two lines restate Q in expanded form and F, the comparison that yields the 16|(a-1)(b-2) criterion.
errors: The conjectured exact formulas A=(p-1)/8+b/4, B=(p-1)/8-b/4 (hence 2B-A=(p-1)/8-3b/4 for 1+i) are false in general. They give the 1+i character correctly only when 16 | (a-1)(b-2); the first prime counterexample is 5+4i (p=41: actual A=4, B=6). Gauss himself flags this ('ist falsch ...', '5+4i').
A-B=b/2 is not exact in general (41: A-B=-2) but holds mod 4, which is all that matters for the character of 2.
The struck-out floor-sum formula A-B=½ab-4Σ[(2k-1)a/2b] is not exact (gives 6 for 5+4i vs true -2), though congruent mod 4. Gauss deleted it.

The second 'allgemeiner' form, -1/8aa+1/4ab-3/8bb-7/8 as transcribed, differs from the first by (a^2+1)/2 ≡ 1 mod 4, so it cannot be the 1+i exponent. Either a misreading (e.g. a constant +1/8 would make it ≡ E1 mod 4) or it refers to something else.

The side congruences '¼bb ≡ b', '¼ab ≡ ½b' do not hold literally as integer congruences mod 2 or 4 for all admissible b (e.g. b=2). They are presumably shorthand used inside the 1/8-fractions; the reading is uncertain.
In the heading the image appears to show '4z^4'; the norm form of Q(2^(1/3)) requires 4z^3 (slip of the pen or of the reading).

results.what: Units of Z[2^(1/3)] (solutions of x^3+2y^3+4z^3-6xyz=1) should be expressible through the sum of a cubic-character L-series Σ ε^n/(m^2+3n^2) over Eisenstein integers.
results.modern_name: Analytic class number formula for the pure cubic field Q(2^(1/3)): ζ_K = ζ·L(χ)·L(χ̄) with a cubic Hecke character, regulator from the fundamental unit 1+θ+θ^2
results.usually_credited_to: Dirichlet (1840s announcements on cubic forms/units), Eisenstein (1844, forms x^3+ny^3+n^2z^3-3nxyz); full formula for pure cubic fields Dedekind (1900)

results.what: Gauss's lemma for biquadratic residues using a triangular 'quarter system' of the fundamental square of the modulus a+bi; characters of 1+i, 1-i, 2 read off from counts A, B of residues in the two halves of the triangle
results.modern_name: Gauss's lemma in Z[i] (biquadratic Gauss lemma) / lattice-point proof of the supplementary laws
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Nachlass), published analogues by Eisenstein (1844) and later authors

results.what: Biquadratic character of 1+i for a≡1 mod 4, b even: exponent (a-b-1)(a-b+5)/8 mod 4; character of 2: exponent b/2 ≡ ab/2 mod 4
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (stated 1832, Theoria residuorum biquadraticorum II); first published proofs Eisenstein 1844

results.what: Criterion that the naive formula (p-1)/8-3b/4 gives the 1+i exponent iff 16|(a-1)(b-2), first failure at 5+4i
results.modern_name: Congruence analysis of quadratic forms for character exponents

deep.surprise_reason: The biquadratic material is a working version of Gauss's known (1832-stated) supplementary laws via a Gauss-lemma count; it is valuable but expected in his Nachlass. The top note is more notable. It explicitly links the unit equation of Q(2^(1/3)) to a cubic L-series over m^2+3n^2, anticipating the analytic class number formula for pure cubic fields usually associated with Dirichlet/Eisenstein and completed by Dedekind (1900). It is only a one-line expectation, and its date and publication status (possibly printed in Werke) are unknown, so the rating stays moderate.

transcription_corrections: Heading: the image seems to read '4z^4' (or a deformed 3); mathematically it must be 4z^3 (norm form of Q(2^(1/3))).
Line 2: Gauss's correction reads 'jenes [a] nach Mod. 4, dieses [b] nach mod 2', replacing 'beides nach Mod. 4'.

Marginal note after A=..., B=...: the sense (confirmed by computation) is that the formula 'ist falsch' unless (a-1)(b-2) is divisible by 16. Equivalently it is wrong when ¼(a-1) is odd and ½b even, the first case being 5+4i ('dann bei 5+4i'). The fragment '3. ... bei -3' is probably 'zum ersten mal bei ...'; exact wording uncertain.
'ein Vierthel der Zahl nach ¼(p-1)' should be read as 'ein Viertel, der Zahl nach ¼(p-1)' (a quarter, namely (p-1)/4 in number).
The second 'allgemeiner' expression '-1/8aa+1/4ab-3/8bb-7/8' should be rechecked against the image. As read it is ≡ (first form) - 1 mod 4; a constant +1/8 would make the two forms equivalent mod 4.
Bottom line '1/8 aa + 1/8 bb - 3/4 b - 1/8' equals (p-1)/8 - 3b/4, the earlier 2B-A expression, written out for comparison with the correct quantity.
